stem:
Rohan studies the diagram of a $3$ by $3$ grid. Each cell must hold a different number from $1$ through $9$. The outside numbers are the sums of their rows or columns.

Which two claims correctly state how the grid may be filled or rejected?

options.text: Any nine integers may fill the cells, even with repeats, if the printed outside sums look large.
Each outside number must equal the sum of its own row or column using the distinct entries $1$ through $9$.
All three row sums together equal $45$, and all three column sums together also equal $45$, because $1+\cdots+9=45$.
The numbers $1$ through $9$ are what create the $3$ by $3$ grid shape itself.

teacher.key_rationale: Distinct 1–9 fill the cells; each outside total is that row or column sum, and the three row sums (and three column sums) total 45. Allowing repeats omits the fill rule; saying 1–9 create the grid shape reverses the relation.
teacher.figure_note: Added 3-by-3 grid with some filled cells and outside row/column sum labels.

mx_swap.reason: Diagonal magic-square scope not sayable with row/column-sum stem objects; kept condition_omission and relationship_reversal on wrong letters.
